title: Brown Dwarfs, Free-Floating Planets and the Bottom of the Initial Mass Function Against the Frame's Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Nikos Nikolaidis, and this is Brown Dwarfs, Free-Floating Planets and the Bottom of the Initial Mass Function Against the Frame's Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Nikos Nikolaidis, and this is Brown Dwarfs, Free-Floating Planets and the Bottom of the Initial Mass Function Against the Frame's Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Accretion and Disk Lifetimes at Substellar Masses'. Its stated result: Headline computed result: tau_002 = 5.2; tau_008 = 3.0; tau_03 = 1.8; Mdot_002 = 6.3e-11. This study is simulated and computed, not measured; every value is reproduced by the deposited compute.py and recorded in results.json.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Brown Dwarf Cooling Tracks: Luminosity and Effective Temperature from 0.1 to 10 Gigayears'. Its stated result: Headline computed result: L_30Mjup_5Gyr = 1.92e-06; Teff_30Mjup_5Gyr = 717; L_75Mjup_5Gyr = 1.32e-05; Teff_75Mjup_5Gyr = 1160; fading_factor_30 = 133.0. This study is simulated and computed, not measured; every value is reproduced by the deposited compute.py and recorded in results.json.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Detection Completeness for Cold Brown Dwarfs in Deep Infrared Surveys'. Its stated result: Headline computed result: comp_500K_10pc = 1.00; comp_350K_10pc = 1.00; comp_350K_5pc = 1.00; comp_700K_20pc = 1.00. This study is simulated and computed, not measured; every value is reproduced by the deposited compute.py and recorded in results.json.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Direct-Imaging Contrast Limits Converted to Companion Mass Limits'. Its stated result: Headline computed result: Mlim_100Myr_1e5 = 12.0; Mlim_100Myr_1e6 = 5.4; Mlim_1Gyr_1e6 = 15.1. This study is simulated and computed, not measured; every value is reproduced by the deposited compute.py and recorded in results.json.
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Effective Temperature and Surface Gravity Degeneracy in Brown Dwarf Spectral Fitting'. Its stated result: Headline computed result: bias_half_dex = 90; bias_1200_logg45 = -90; valley_slope_K_per_dex = 180. This study is simulated and computed, not measured; every value is reproduced by the deposited compute.py and recorded in results.json.
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Ejection Versus Direct Formation: Velocity and Multiplicity Signatures of Free-Floating Planets'. Its stated result: Headline computed result: retained_sigma2 = 0.20; retained_sigma5 = 0.02; escaped_sigma5 = 0.98. This study is simulated and computed, not measured; every value is reproduced by the deposited compute.py and recorded in results.json.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Accretion and Disk Lifetimes at Substellar Masses”. Its stated result is: Headline computed result: tau_002 = 5.2; tau_008 = 3.0; tau_03 = 1.8; Mdot_002 = 6.3e-11. This study is simulated and computed, not measured; every value is reproduced by the deposited compute.py and recorded in results.json. (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Accretion and Disk Lifetimes at Substellar Masses'; 'Brown Dwarf Cooling Tracks: Luminosity and Effective Temperature from 0.1 to 10 Gigayears'; 'Detection Completeness for Cold Brown Dwarfs in Deep Infrared Surveys'; 'Direct-Imaging Contrast Limits Converted to Companion Mass Limits'; 'Effective Temperature and Surface Gravity Degeneracy in Brown Dwarf Spectral Fitting'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

And here is that same result with the words stripped away — just the quantities standing in a row: tau_002 = 5.2; tau_008 = 3.0; tau_03 = 1.8. Find tau_002 in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'Accretion and Disk Lifetimes at Substellar Masses' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: tau_002 = 5.2; tau_008 = 3.0; tau_03 = 1.8. (3) This question asks for the value paired with tau_002. (4) In that row, tau_002 stands beside 5.2 — so the answer the lesson gives is 5.2. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.
questions.q: In the lesson, the paper 'Accretion and Disk Lifetimes at Substellar Masses' reported a number for tau_002. What number did it report?
questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
